title: Remember When It Matters: Proactive Memory Agent for Long-Horizon Agents
authors: Yifan Wu, Lizhu Zhang, Yuhang Zhou, Mingyi Wang, Bo Peng, Serena Li, Xiangjun Fan, Zhuokai Zhao
date: submitted 9 July 2026 (arXiv v1, the only version; the paper's own date line says 24 August 2026)

code.title: yifannnwu/proactive-memory-agent
code.note: Apache-2.0. The memory agent (both phases, the four bank tools, the trigger), the Terminal-Bench runner on a vendored Harbor with Enroot sandboxes, the two run configurations, and five rendered example traces (baseline and memory run of the same task). Not released: the τ²-Bench runs, the ablation variants, the SETA training code and the trained Qwen3.5-27B memory agent (checked 3 October 2026)

takeaway: A second model runs beside an unmodified action agent, keeps a small structured memory bank of the run, and at each step either injects a reminder into the actor's next call or stays silent. With Claude Opus 4.6 as that memory agent, Claude Sonnet 4.5 goes from 37.6% to 45.9% on Terminal-Bench 2.0 and from 55.0% to 61.8% on τ²-Bench; Opus 4.6 itself gains 2.4 and 2.5 points; a frozen Qwen3.5-122B-A10B actor gains 37.6% to 41.1% on Terminal-Bench with a Qwen3.5-27B memory agent trained by SFT and GRPO.
verdict: Believe that a strong second model watching a weaker one helps it, clearly on τ²-Bench and probably on Terminal-Bench. Do not take the title's claim, that knowing when to stay silent is what helps, as shown: every number is a single run, always reminding solves 171 τ²-Bench tasks against 170 and 172 for two runs of the selective agent, the Terminal-Bench baseline sits 5 points under Sonnet 4.5's published score, and in the five released traces the memory agent speaks at 65% of steps, mostly with fresh debugging advice rather than reminders, at an estimated cost about equal to the actor's.
